blocks.title: The Palais–Smale condition
blocks.content:
Nicolas Freches, Henrik Schumacher, Daniel Steenebrügge, and Heiko von der Mosel
Institute for Mathematics, RWTH Aachen University
March 3, 2026
Abstract
We prove that various families of energies relevant in geometric knot theory satisfy
the Palais–Smale condition (PS) on submanifolds of arclength parametrized knots. These
energies include linear combinations of the Euler-Bernoulli bending energy with a wide
variety of non-local knot energies, such as O’Hara’s self-repulsive potentials 𝐸𝛼,𝑝, gen-
eralized tangent-point energies TP( 𝑝,𝑞), and generalized integral Menger curvature func-

1.1. The Palais–Smale condition
A Palais–Smale sequence (or (PS)-sequence) for a continuously differentiable energy function
E on a smooth Banach manifold M, is a sequence (𝑥𝑘)𝑘⊂M such that sup𝑘∈N E(𝑥𝑘) < ∞
and lim𝑘→∞∥DE𝑥𝑘∥(𝑇𝑥𝑘M)∗= 0, where (𝑇𝑥M)∗denotes the dual space of the tangent space
𝑇𝑥M of the manifold M at the point 𝑥∈M.

sequence (𝑥𝑘)𝑘⊂M for E contains a convergent subsequence, 𝑥𝑘𝑙→𝑥∞∈M as 𝑙→∞.

blocks.title: Tangent-point energy
blocks.content:
\label{sec:tanpoint}

The most difficult case is when the energy is a pure self-avoidance energy,
which naturally has a non-local structure so that now the leading order
terms are of fractional Sobolev regularity. We 
concentrate here on the tangent-point energies $\TP^{(p,2)}$ for
the range $p\in (4,5)$. 
As shown in \cite[Theorem 1.1]{blatt-reiter_2015a},
the underlying energy spaces are the Hilbert
spaces $H^{1+s}(\Circle,\AmbSpace)$ with $s \ceq (p-3)/2$.

Here we gather a few product rules, i.e., statements of well-definedness and existence of bilinear
compositions of functions in certain Sobolev classes. We use these results throughout the main
body of the work, in particular, for the regularity theory in Section 5.
We start with the following result, which can be found as Theorem 7.4 in [8] but is included
here for the reader’s convenience. Notice that this theorem for bounded Lipschitz domains can
be generalized to compact smooth manifolds such as R/Z by the usual tricks of the trade such
